text_blocks.snippet: Losartan is a prescription medication used to treat high blood pressure and protect kidney function, but it can cause both mild and serious side effects.
These symptoms are usually mild and often improve over time as your body adjusts to the medication:

list.snippet: Dizziness or lightheadedness (especially when standing up quickly)
Upper respiratory infections or stuffy nose
Mild digestive issues like nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea

text_blocks.snippet: Though rare, some side effects require medical attention or emergency care:

list.snippet: High potassium levels (Hyperkalemia): Can cause muscle weakness, confusion, or an irregular heartbeat.
Low blood pressure (Hypotension): Can lead to severe dizziness, fainting, or blurred vision.
Kidney problems: Signs include a sudden decrease in urination, swelling in the hands, ankles, or feet, or unexplained weight gain.
Allergic reaction (Angioedema): A life-threatening emergency causing swelling of the face, lips, tongue, throat, or trouble breathing.
Pregnancy warning: Losartan should not be taken during pregnancy as it can cause serious injury or death to an unborn baby.

text_blocks.snippet: You can learn more details about indications and safety via MedlinePlus Losartan or the Mayo Clinic Losartan Guide.
